facts: The Warriors overcame a 20-point second-half deficit to beat the Los Angeles Lakers 101-89 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Tuesday.
The Dubs turned the tide with defense, forcing 30 Laker turnovers and recording 20 steals.
Offensively, four starters scored in double figures, with Brandin Podziemski and Yaxel Lendeborg scoring 17 points each, Stephen Curry adding 11, and Gui Santos adding 10.
The Lakers also had four starters in double figures, paced by Austin Reaves’ 28 points, but Golden State forced Reaves to commit seven turnovers.
The Warriors outscored the Lakers by 16 points in the decisive fourth quarter, 29-13.
WARRIORS OVERCOME 20-POINT DEFICIT The Warriors trailed by as many as 20 points in the third quarter but chipped away and eventually took the lead in the fourth.
They scored 13 unanswered points to cut the deficit to seven and were within four at the end of the third quarter.
Brandin Podziemski opened the fourth quarter with a pair of jumpers that tied the game at 76.
